A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EvoPress despite the revised title and formatting. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments, perplexity and zero-shot accuracy results, convergence measurements, and ablations across depth pruning, sparsity, and quantization.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds seed-robustness results, constrained quantization results, and runtime comparisons in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The level database, KL-divergence fitness, level-switch mutation, and multistage selection remain unchanged. Appendix G adds an early-stopping variant and a two-stage EvoPress+BESA procedure that refines EvoPress-derived block sparsities through rowwise allocation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same calibration and evaluation corpora and the same language-model compression tasks, including the five zero-shot benchmarks. The added runtime studies, Wanda implementation, and vLLM precision restrictions change configurations and procedures within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds evaluated comparisons against SLEB and BlockPruner for depth pruning and against layerwise and rowwise BESA for sparsity allocation. These substantially expand comparison with competing search procedures beyond v1's baseline set; the original comparisons remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: The original Table 8 settings remain, but substantial additional protocols appear: 1000-generation seed experiments, stopping after 20 generations without training-perplexity improvement, Wanda-based sparsity comparisons, and vLLM-compatible 4/8-bit search with coupled projection precisions. Table 17 adds runtime and forward-pass measurements on an RTX 4090. These are additional settings, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds seed sensitivity and configuration-consistency analyses in Appendix C.2, and tests layerwise perplexity prediction when removing 2, 4, or 6 blocks in Appendix D.4. Table 18 also examines combining EvoPress with BESA. These materially extend robustness and mechanism validation beyond the retained mutation, selection, and fitness ablations.

E5.justification: v1 contains no empirical repeated-seed uncertainty study. v2 reports 16 independent runs, standard-deviation bands in Figure 7, and mean C4 perplexity 33.82 with standard deviation 0.61 for Llama-3-8B at 70% sparsity. This substantial addition is confined to the new robustness study; uncertainty is not added throughout the benchmark tables.

E6.justification: Most matched original scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Figures 4, 6, 7, and 10 and Tables 17–18. For example, Table 17 reports C4 perplexity/runtime of 19.87/53 minutes for EvoPress versus 20.91/159 minutes for SLEB at 37.5% depth pruning. Conversely, Tables 2–3 lose individual task scores for compressed models and the Llama-3.1 compressed-model rows, without restoring those scores in the appendices.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 becomes Theorem 3.1, retaining the linear-fitness assumptions and expected O(k(n-k)/lambda) convergence bound. Appendix A preserves the supporting definitions, lemmas, and drift proofs. Changes are numbering, typography, and explanatory wording.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a unified, efficient evolutionary framework for three compression approaches, a convergence guarantee for linear fitness, and competitive compression quality across the same model families. The rewritten abstract and conclusion alter emphasis without substantively changing these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the monotonicity argument by describing useful prediction at low compression and deterioration at medium sparsity. It also interprets seed consistency as evidence against problematic local optima and explains EvoPress–BESA complementarity. Appendix G adds qualifications about runtime/data tradeoffs, differing sparsity granularity, and incomplete tuning-cost accounting.

D1.justification: v2 adds RTX 4090 hardware information for Table 17, runtime-accounting exclusions for BESA, and vLLM precision/grouping requirements. Figure 3 newly clarifies minibatch fitness versus full-test-set perplexity measurement. The original hyperparameter table and code URL remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SLEB, BlockPruner, BESA, Wanda, and straight-through estimation, and positions BESA as complementary to EvoPress. The Kwon et al. reference is removed. The main related-work organization and unified-compression novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, several passages and the conclusion are shortened, and the baseline list becomes prose. Appendix C gains subsections, Appendix G and an impact statement are added, and the contents page disappears. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference layout. Tables 2–3 are substantially condensed; Figure 2 loses its profile panel and changes its vertical scale. New quantization, seed-robustness, and correlation figures and runtime tables are added, while numerous retained displays are resized, reordered, or redrawn.

improvement.justification: The 16-seed study addresses an important reliability gap for stochastic search, while comparisons against competing search methods substantially strengthen evidence for practical efficiency. The added low-compression analysis also clarifies the motivating argument's limits. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed scores in Tables 2–3, although runtime comparisons retain stated comparability limits and Figure 4 does not quantify its claimed vLLM speedups.
